governanceNotes: D1 batch 40 (2026-09-23): deferred as a class/umbrella identity (duplicate-scope guard; gastrointestinal-cancers batch 37, diabetes-mellitus batch 22, eczema batch 27, female-reproductive-disorders batch 33 precedents). The identity is catalogued under Infectious & Tropical Diseases as the generic label 'Granulomatous disease' spanning granulomatous inflammation of infectious, immune, and foreign-body etiology. Condition-specific member and sibling identities already exist and own their respective windows: tuberculosis (published, two outgoing associations to aortic-aneurysm and bronchiectasis), histoplasmosis (zero-edge backlog identity with its own upcoming window), sarcoidosis (published, two outgoing associations), and granuloma-annulare (deferred batch 39 with a recorded direction-inverted screen) - authoring outgoing edges from the umbrella label would assert parallel pathways beneath identities that own them (parallel-pathway ban). No condition-specific quantified forward-outcome cohort exists for the umbrella label itself: outcomes of 'granulomatous disease' as a class (infection dissemination, organ failure, scarring) are necessarily the outcomes of the specific underlying granulomatous diagnoses, and attributing them to the umbrella would double-count every member chain (duplicate-mediated guard; zero-record guard). Negative screens recorded: no fever, weight-loss, or fatigue constitutional edge (symptom-level, no umbrella-specific quantification, wrong-identity guard); no sepsis or organ-failure edge (member-diagnosis mediated, and no sepsis identity fits); no malignancy edge (chronic-inflammation cancer risk lacks umbrella-specific quantification in this window). Reopening condition: if governance reclassifies the identity to a specific granulomatous diagnosis, or if a quantified outcomes cohort for the umbrella label independent of member diagnoses is published; member-diagnosis windows proceed on their own schedule regardless.
